name: Shellbreak Day
description: Observed on the anniversary of the 2201 Nakamura-Osei Riots, when the Gray Zone residents of the Calumet Flats district destroyed three Veridian Corp automated eviction drones and held the block for eleven days before corporate security retook it. The holiday is marked by leaving cracked shells — real or sculpted from scrap — on doorsteps and window ledges as a symbol of forced emergence. No one got out clean, but they got out together.
cultural_impact: Shellbreak Day has quietly normalized the idea of collective resistance as a form of community identity in the Gray Zone, and the cracked-shell iconography appears year-round in the Gray Zone graffiti, tattoos, and market stalls. Tier 2 workers often observe it privately with a shared meal, rarely speaking its name aloud near corp-monitored spaces.
locations: Calumet Flats, South the Gray Zone
story_hooks: A Tier 3 journalist discovers their own grandparent was one of the Calumet Eleven and must decide whether to publish the story or bury it to protect living family members still under corporate employment contracts.
Veridian Corp hires a fixer to quietly document and photograph everyone leaving shells on their doorsteps this year — a player character is on that list.

Someone is manufacturing perfect ceramic shells stamped with a hidden data chip containing the full unredacted security footage from the 2201 riots, and distributing them through ghost markets before the holiday.
origin_event: The eleven-day occupation of Calumet Flats Block 7 during the 2201 Nakamura-Osei Riots, named for the two families who first barricaded their doors against automated eviction units.
tier_observations: Tier 1 residents leave cracked shells on stoops, share communal meals of whatever is available, and hold unlicensed music gatherings after dark. Tier 2 workers observe quietly with a shared drink or private meal, rarely using the holiday's name near monitored spaces. Tier 3 and above are largely unaware it exists, or dismiss it as 'the Gray Zone superstition.' Tier 4-5 security forces are placed on elevated alert on this date every year without being told why.
